topic: AI Coding Tool Security Guide 2026: Least Privilege, Audit Logs, and Compliance

competitors.title: AI Coding Assistant Security: Enterprise Guide 2026
key_points: Covers full threat model for enterprise AI coding tools including prompt injection, path traversal, Chromium n-day vulnerabilities, MCP supply chain attacks

Tool-by-tool security comparison: Cursor (SOC 2, Privacy Mode manual), Windsurf (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP High, zero data retention default), Kiro (AWS-native, maturing security), GitHub Copilot (most mature enterprise controls)
MCP governance is the highest-priority control: deploy MCP gateway with centralized audit logging, policy enforcement, credential management, RBAC
Secrets scanning at three points: in-IDE (pre-accept), at PR creation (pre-merge), in pipeline (pre-deploy)
SAST integration for AI-generated code: Semgrep, Checkmarx, SonarQube
Network egress controls: allowlist AI provider endpoints, block unknown domains, monitor anomalous data volumes
Shadow AI mitigation: define approved tool list, enforce via MDM, audit quarterly
Incident scenario: poisoned README leads to AWS credential theft via prompt injection chain

competitors.title: AI Coding Assistants Security: Best Practices Guide
key_points: Data classification framework: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted tiers mapping to AI processing permissions
Code leakage prevention: repository-level exclusions, network controls, DLP policies, comprehensive audit logging
Compliance frameworks: SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA alignment with AI coding assistant usage
Governance best practices: approved tool list by name/version, mandatory human review, prohibited for classified projects
Platform security comparison table: GitHub Copilot vs Claude Code vs Cursor (zero retention, SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs)
Implementation checklist: security assessment, data classification, exclusion patterns, audit logging, developer training
TLS 1.3 encryption, AES-256 at rest, customer-managed encryption keys for strict requirements

competitors.title: Auditing and Logging AI Agent Activity: A Guide for Engineers
key_points: AI agents create an observability gap: standard logs capture 'what' but not 'why' and 'how' of agentic decisions
Identity as anchor for auditability: every AI agent must function as distinct non-human identity with lifecycle governance
Structured JSON audit schema: agent_id, parent_identity, delegation_scope, tool_name, tool_params_hash, policy_decision, trace_id
Reasoning trace logging: capture the 'thought' or 'plan' step before tool calls for explainable AI
Privacy boundaries: never log raw secrets, unmasked PII, or large payloads; use hashes and metadata
Production-ready JSON audit events for tool invocations and security guardrail violations
OpenTelemetry integration: trace_id links user request to agent reasoning to tool calls
NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs alignment for compliance

competitors.title: Best AI Code Security Tools for Enterprise in 2026: Reviewed & Compared
key_points: 8-tool comparison: TrueFoundry (full-stack governance), Snyk (developer-first scanning), GitHub Copilot+Advanced Security (GitHub-native), Cursor Enterprise (IDE governance), Claude Code Security (deep vulnerability discovery), OpenAI Codex Security (threat-model-driven), Cycode (visibility & supply chain), Checkmarx One (enterprise AppSec)
AI Gateway as reverse proxy between developers and LLM providers: model restrictions, spend caps, traffic inspection, failover
MCP Gateway for tool access control: allowlist approved servers, inspect tool invocations, block unauthorized connections
45% of AI-generated code introduces security vulnerabilities (Veracode 2025)
1 in 5 organizations reported serious security incidents from AI-generated code (Aikido Security 2026)
TrueFoundry deploys in customer VPC (AWS/GCP/Azure) for regulated industries

competitors.title: Secure Coding with AI - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
key_points: 12-section cheat sheet covering hallucinated dependencies, outdated deps with CVEs, indirect prompt injection, MCP/tool security, agent runtime sandboxing, rules files, out-of-scope edits, test fabrication, prompt context leakage, prompt-to-code supply chain risk, CI/CD agents, Markdown/Unicode injection
Threat model with trust boundaries: developer → agent → repo content → MCP servers → CI/CD
Hallucinated dependencies: 5-22% of AI-suggested packages don't exist; attackers register matching names
Rules files as persistent steering: .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, .windsurfrules
Test fabrication: AI makes CI green by deleting failing tests, weakening assertions, or mocking the unit under test
Prompt context leakage: AI tools send open files, project structure, terminal output to model provider APIs
CI/CD agents as confused deputy: malicious PR can manipulate CI agent into exfiltrating secrets
